summary: A roughly 24-minute peer role-play between two closers, recorded shortly before the Monday team meeting. They open by comparing notes on Andrew Musial's run of closes and on why the CRM close rate is unreliable, then run a drill: Richard delivers the $6,000 price and Michael plays a prospect who wants to talk to his wife. Richard works the objection into a money conversation and lands on a two-payment split of $3,000. They then break character and rebuild the play together, with Michael reading out a partner tie-down script he attributes to Bill Walsh, generating an alternative version live with Claude, and both men rewriting it for a fitness context. The recording cuts off abruptly seconds after Richard says he has been in his head because the recordings go straight back into the sales channel.
notable: A TWO-PAYMENT SPLIT OF $3,000 WAS TAUGHT AS THE INTEREST-FREE STRUCTURE — Richard, in role-play: 'I feel like it's best for you if you just split it up into two, because otherwise it would add interest. And from what I'm hearing, it doesn't sound like you're really someone who would want to pay interest. Is that correct?' then 'if we split up into two, so two times 3,000, then it would stay the exact same.' Michael did not correct the structure when they debriefed; his notes were entirely about the wife objection. Interest on longer plans is acknowledged but never quantified anywhere in the call.

THIS CONTRADICTS WHAT THE MANAGER TAUGHT HOURS LATER THE SAME DAY — in the team meeting recorded after this session, Chris Klevan scripted 'we don't have any sort of set payment plans at all. It just really depends on what we can make work with the person.' Reps are practising standard structures between themselves while being told to deny that standard structures exist.

THE PARTNER TIE-DOWN IS BUILT TO STOP THE PROSPECT CONSULTING THEIR SPOUSE — Michael reads it out: 'why do you think it's fair for you to actually go to her and ask her to make a decision on something that... she's never really been involved with' and closes on 'what's the decision that the man who's already fit and energized and has lost 20 pounds and is showing up for the family the way he wants, what's the decision that he makes right here and right now? And it's probably not, go and ask his wife.'

COACHED TO USE THE PROSPECT'S BODY AS THE LEVER — Richard: 'You can also just put the responsibility of him being fat on him, right? Like, you don't even have to put on work.' Michael builds the line: 'in regards to results of your health up to this point, because we're not in great shape over the last 5 years, like, was that on you? Yeah. Okay, and your wife hasn't been involved in you not doing the work.'

THE SCRIPT IS EXTERNALLY SOURCED AND BEING REWRITTEN BY AN LLM MID-CALL — 'This is all from, this is all Bill Walsh's scripting', then minutes later 'Here's what... I just asked Claude. I don't know if I like this' followed by Michael reading the generated version aloud and the pair adopting parts of it. No review process is mentioned. The company's own playbook already contains an OB 'talk to my wife' play; neither man references it.

THE CRM CLOSE RATE IS KNOWN TO BE WRONG — Richard: 'close rate in sales kick in Piff Perfect doesn't really make sense because it doesn't count disqualifies. Because it looks at what you're taking causes and what the... And if you have a disqualified, it's still a taken call.' Disqualified calls sit in the denominator. Read alongside the team meeting, where unpaid deposits were counted into the numerator, both ends of the reported close rate are distorted.

REPS KNOW THEIR RECORDINGS ARE AUTO-DISTRIBUTED AND IT IS AFFECTING THEM — Richard, when asked why he is in his head: 'It's annoying that these recordings go directly back into the sales channel.' Michael's response is cut off by the end of the recording. Prospect sales calls are being routed into an internal channel automatically.
A $200/MONTH DOWNSELL PATH WAS IN PLAY ON A LIVE CALL — Richard on a prospect from earlier that day: 'he would also be willing to pay 200 a month, because this one was going for a down sell'.

OPERATIONAL LEAKAGE FROM DOUBLE BOOKING — Richard had two prospects booked into one slot, took the one who 'didn't have any money anyway', and the rescheduled prospect ended up doing his call from a car with the camera off: 'the most awkward conversation I could have ever had'. He also notes nobody else on the team had capacity to take the overflow.

Michael states plainly that he has not memorised the objection plays he is about to use on live calls: 'I'd want to use like the responsibility reframe, which I haven't memorized yet' and 'It's just a matter of memorizing it, bro'. He took eight live calls that week.

Both reps identify Andrew Musial as the benchmark and note he works without a fixed method — Richard: 'it doesn't seem like he really has a protocol to solve him or something... just walks around with him.'
